thread:
Cheng: Quick callout - saw a perf regression on prefill after the kernel routing tweak. Prefill for rdlw-7b dropped ~25% on A100-80G when we started re-evaluating kernel at prefill->decode boundary.

Mira: Do you have the raw numbers and config?

Cheng: Sure. seq=2048 prefill, decode=512. Before the change: prefill throughput ~12.3k tok/s, p99 ~180ms. After: prefill ~9.1k tok/s, p99 ~240ms. Host CPU and GPU profiler both show a sync around kv_commit at the handoff.

Sam: Can you paste the profiler excerpt? My hunch is we're toggling to a paged kernel late in prefill.

Cheng: nvprof hot list (trimmed):
```
Time(ms)  Kernel                          Calls
1200      flash_attn_forward_v2            1
480       paged_attention_fused_kernel     6
230       kv_cache_commit_kernel           1  <-- spike
```
Note multiple small paged launches at the end of prefill which we didn't see before.

Anya: What is the routing policy now? We recently added kv_pages into the decision.

Cheng: Policy: if seq_len>1024 or kv_pages>8 -> prefer paged-fusion, else flashattn-v2. The issue: we evaluate policy again during the prefill->decode transition, so for some requests we end up re-binding which forces a sync on kv_commit.

Mira: So continuous batching plus very small decode batches could flip the decision mid-request. That would explain the sudden sync.

Cheng: Exactly. With continuous batching enabled, prefill merges many inflight requests. When the head finishes prefill and starts decode (tiny decode batch), policy sees a smaller batch and requests flashattn, triggering kernelCtor and a blocking reorder.

Sam: We should avoid mid-request kernel reinit. Options: sticky kernel per request, short TTL for selection, defer rebind until after commit, or warm both kernels.

Anya: I propose: 1) pick kernel at prefill using projected decode batch (projected_decode = max(1, floor(prefill_batch * decode_to_prefill_ratio))) and 2) add a no-rebind window (e.g., 200-300ms) that prevents switches during commit.

PerfBot: quick harness numbers:
```
config A (baseline): prefill 12.3k tok/s, end-to-end 8.9k tok/s
config B (new routing, rebind allowed): prefill 9.1k tok/s, end-to-end 7.4k tok/s
config C (sticky selection + no-rebind): prefill 11.8k tok/s, end-to-end 8.6k tok/s
```

Mira: Good signal. Can you capture a microtrace (nsight) to see memcpy/launch ordering?

Cheng: nsight timeline shows a ~2.3ms gap where CPU issues kv_commit then waits for kernel init callback. kernelCtor path does device-side memsets which look to block until completion.

Sam: kernelCtor is likely the heavy hitter. Short-term mitigation: sticky selection with TTL. Mid-term: evaluate warming both kernels for hot models. Longer-term: make commit async with events so rebind waits on an event instead of blocking.

Anya: Warming both kernels increases memory usage on Dedicated nodes. But we can restrict warming to hot model whitelist. I'll run a memory impact estimate across top-10 models.

Cheng: I experimented with event-based deferral (cudaEventRecord + cudaStreamWaitEvent) to schedule the rebind after commit. It reduced p99 by ~35% in the local harness but some runtime code expects commit to be synchronous; that needs careful auditing.

Sam: Let's land a conservative fix first. Plan: implement sticky per-request kernel affinity with TTL=250ms, add unit tests asserting request-local ordering and no mid-request kernel_switch, and add a console metric kernel_switch_count by request_id. Then iterate on the async path.

Mira: Agreed. Action items: 
- Cheng: PR for sticky selection + TTL=250ms, include unit/integration test for kv ordering (EOD).
- Sam: Prototype async event-based rebind in a branch, run full perf/regression suite (due Thursday).
- Anya: Memory cost assessment for warming both kernels for top-10 hot models (EOD tomorrow).
- InfraBot: schedule canary 'ded-prefill-canary' once Cheng's PR lands.

InfraBot: created canary job ded-prefill-canary (run id #7722). Will post results here.

PerfBot: canary trial: sticky-selection reduced the regression to ~4% throughput loss vs baseline; p99 within ~8% of baseline.

Mira: Solid. Ship sticky selection as mitigation; follow up with warming/async research.

Cheng: I'll open the PR and include perf logs + a tiny Console metric for kernel_switch_count/request_id. Also adding an Optimize eval to simulate small-batch decode patterns so routing changes get caught earlier.

Anya: Please add that Optimize eval to the top-of-tree regression harness.

Sam: Noted. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Cheng: PR will land shortly, posting link when ready.
